summary: The fleet array; at least one vehicle is required. Each entry is a vehicle with capacity, skills, shift, and anchors.
range: Array of vehicle objects; length >= 1. Each requires id.

constraints.text: Required field; at least one vehicle must be present.
Each vehicle object must have a mandatory 'id' field (string or integer).

validationRules.text: Missing or empty vehicles array -> HTTP 400.
A vehicle without an 'id' field -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: one well-formed vehicle with id and capacity.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: vehicles is an array of vehicle objects

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: empty vehicles array [] -> HTTP 400.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: at least one vehicle required

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: vehicle missing 'id' field -> HTTP 400.
Positive: three vehicles with distinct ids (1, 2, 3) and no id duplicates.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: unique IDs required per vehicle

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle id as integer (10) and another as string ("veh_A") in same request.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: id can be either string or integer (oneOf)

summary: Zones the vehicle may serve tasks in. Empty array restricts to zone-less tasks only. Omission allows all zones.
range: Array of integer zone IDs. Empty array restricts vehicle to only zone-less tasks. Omission = unlimited.

businessRules.text: Empty allowed_zones restricts the vehicle to tasks with no zone assignment.
A task in a non-allowed zone cannot be served by this vehicle.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: allowed_zones [1, 2] serves jobs in zones [1] or [2].
testingGuidance.rationale: zone-eligibility rule: vehicle allowed in zone matches job zone

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: job in zone 5 with no vehicle allowed there -> unassigned (zone reason).
testingGuidance.rationale: zone-eligibility rule: task in non-allowed zone

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: allowed_zones empty array [] with a zoned job -> unassigned.
testingGuidance.rationale: zone-eligibility rule: empty allowed_zones means zone-less tasks only

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle allowed_zones [1] serves job with zones [1].
Negative-infeasible: every vehicle restricts zone 2, but job requires zone 2 -> unassigned.
Interaction: allowed_zones and restricted_zones both set on same vehicle; a task in allowed but not restricted can be served.
testingGuidance.rationale: zone-eligibility: must check both allowed and restricted

summary: Alternate capacity configurations the vehicle can adopt (the solver picks one at optimization time).
range: Array of integer arrays; each inner array has the SAME dimension count as capacity. Cannot be shared/merged across vehicles.

constraints.text: Each inner array's length must equal the dimension count of vehicles.capacity.

validationRules.text: Dimension mismatch between an alternative_capacity array and the primary capacity -> HTTP 400 input validation failed.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: capacity [100] with alternative_capacities [[80], [150]] — solver picks best fit.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: alt configs used for flexible capacity

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: capacity [10, 100] but an alternative [[5]] (1-D vs 2-D) -> HTTP 400 dimension mismatch.
Positive: capacity [10, 100] with alternative_capacities [[8, 90], [15, 120]] — all 2-D, dimensions consistent.
Boundary: alternative_capacities with same values as primary capacity [[10, 100]] — logically redundant but valid.
Negative-validation: capacity [100] but min_stop_load [5, 10] (1-D vs 2-D) in same vehicle -> HTTP 400.
testingGuidance.rationale: capacity-dimension-consistency: min_stop_load dimension must match capacity

summary: Mandatory driver breaks scheduled within permitted windows; appear as break steps in the route.
range: Array of break objects. Only ONE of breaks / layover_config allowed per vehicle.

constraints.text: Cannot be combined with layover_config on the same vehicle.

businessRules.text: Each break must be scheduled inside one of its time_windows, which must lie within the vehicle's shift.
All breaks are treated as mandatory; if feasible, all will be part of the route.

validationRules.text: Both breaks and layover_config set on the same vehicle -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: one lunch break with time_windows [43200, 46800] inside the vehicle's 09:00–17:00 shift.
Negative-validation: breaks and layover_config both specified -> HTTP 400.
Negative-infeasible: a break window entirely outside the vehicle's time_window -> unschedulable.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: break windows must fit within shift

testingGuidance.text: Positive: two breaks each with non-overlapping time_windows, both inside the shift.
Interaction: a long break duration (1 hour) increases working time; combined with max_working_time cap can breach limit.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: break service counts toward max_working_time

summary: Multi-dimensional maximum load a vehicle can carry. Cumulative onboard load must never exceed capacity on any dimension at any point along the route.
range: Array of non-negative integers, one value per load dimension (e.g. [weight, volume, pallets]). No fixed upper bound in the spec.

constraints.text: Dimension count must stay consistent with jobs[].delivery, jobs[].pickup, and shipments[].amount.

businessRules.text: Hard constraint: for every dimension d, running onboard load <= capacity[d] at every step of the route.
Pickups increase load mid-route, so a load that is feasible at the depot can still breach capacity between a pickup and its delivery.
When violated, the offending task is placed in result.unassigned[] with a capacity reason; the solve still returns HTTP 200 and result.code == 0.

validationRules.text: Inconsistent dimension lengths across capacity/delivery/pickup/amount -> HTTP 400 input validation failed.
Negative capacity value like [-5] -> HTTP 400 input validation failed.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: capacity [100] with a single delivery [40] -> onboard load <= 100 at every step.
Boundary: demand exactly equal to capacity (delivery [50] on capacity [50]) fits.
Positive: multi-dimension capacity [10, 100] with all deliveries/pickups/amounts 2-D and within both bounds -> accepted.
Negative-validation: negative capacity value like [-5] -> HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: dimension mismatch (capacity [10, 100] but a job delivery [5]) -> HTTP 400.
Negative-infeasible: a single job whose delivery exceeds every vehicle's capacity -> in result.unassigned (capacity reason), still HTTP 200, result.code 0.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: unservable load goes to unassigned

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: capacity [10, 100] with two deliveries [2, 60] + [2, 50] on same vehicle breaches VOLUME (110 > 100) though weight (4 <= 10) is fine -> second job unassigned by volume.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: breach on any dimension blocks assignment

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: N jobs each delivery [1] on capacity [N] all fit; the (N+1)th on the same route breaches -> unassigned.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: cumulative load must not exceed capacity

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: zero-quantity demand [0] is always capacity-feasible (a weightless stop).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: zero load does not consume capacity

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: pickup increases load; if pickup [30] on capacity [50] but next delivery [50], running load becomes 50+30=80 > 50 -> infeasible between pickup and delivery.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: pickups raise onboard load mid-route

summary: Per-vehicle cost configuration shaping which vehicle the solver prefers (soft — never forces infeasibility).
range: Object: { fixed?, per_hour?, per_km?, per_order?, min_stop_load_*_penalty?, deadhead_*_penalty? }.

businessRules.text: Costs steer selection/ordering but never violate a hard constraint or force an otherwise-servable task unassigned.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: fixed 500 + per_km 10 makes a cheaper vehicle preferred.
Behavioral: raising fixed cost discourages using an extra vehicle.
Positive: per_order 50 balances fulfilling more orders against the per-order surcharge.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_order always added to route cost

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: high deadhead_distance_penalty reduces empty-leg distance; pairs with max_deadhead_distance.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: deadhead penalty steers empty-travel behavior

summary: Penalty per unit of deadhead (empty-leg) distance beyond max_deadhead_distance.
range: Integer. Default 0.

businessRules.text: Soft: discourages long empty first/last legs; pairs with max_deadhead_distance.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: high penalty (e.g., 100) reduces empty-travel distance.
Positive: penalty 0 (default) applies no cost to deadhead overruns.
Interaction: when max_deadhead_distance 500m is set with deadhead_distance_penalty 50, overages are penalized per meter.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty applies to distance beyond max

summary: Penalty per unit of deadhead (empty-leg) duration beyond max_deadhead_duration.
range: Integer. Default 0.

businessRules.text: Soft: discourages long empty first/last legs; pairs with max_deadhead_duration.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: high penalty pushes vehicles to start/end nearer demand.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty cost discourages idle time

testingGuidance.text: Positive: penalty 0 (default) applies no cost to deadhead time overruns.
Interaction: when max_deadhead_duration 600s is set with deadhead_duration_penalty 75, overages are penalized per second.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty applies to duration beyond max

summary: Fixed cost of using the vehicle at all (added once if the vehicle is used).
range: Integer. Default 0.

businessRules.text: Discourages using an extra vehicle unless it reduces total cost enough.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: high fixed cost (e.g., 1000) -> solver consolidates onto fewer vehicles.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: fixed cost incentivizes vehicle consolidation

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: fixed 0 (no usage penalty) applies no fixed surcharge.
Positive: fixed 500 makes a vehicle economically viable only if demand justifies it.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: fixed cost added per vehicle usage

summary: Fixed penalty applied when any delivery stop's load is below min_stop_load.
range: Integer.

businessRules.text: Triggered per stop that falls short of vehicles.min_stop_load; soft — does not force unassignment.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: a delivery below min_stop_load still served but incurs this fixed penalty.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty applied to low-load stops

testingGuidance.text: Positive: min_stop_load_fixed_penalty 300 discourages inefficient low-load deliveries.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: fixed penalty per underutilized stop

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: when min_stop_load [20] is set with a delivery [5] and min_stop_load_fixed_penalty 100, the stop incurs a 100-unit penalty.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty triggered when delivery < min_stop_load

summary: Per-unit shortfall penalty vs min_stop_load (per dimension).
range: Array of integers, one per capacity dimension.

constraints.text: Same dimension count as min_stop_load / capacity.

businessRules.text: Scales with how far below min_stop_load a delivery falls.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: larger shortfall -> proportionally larger penalty (e.g., shortfall of 10 units at 5 per unit = 50 penalty).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: unit penalty scales with shortfall

testingGuidance.text: Positive: min_stop_load_unit_penalty [10] with a delivery [15] vs min_stop_load [20] incurs (20-15)*10=50 penalty.
Positive: multi-dimensional min_stop_load_unit_penalty [5, 2] with two dimensions; each dimension penalized independently.
Interaction: min_stop_load [50, 100] with delivery [40, 80] and penalties [10, 5] incurs (50-40)*10 + (100-80)*5 = 100 + 100 = 200 total penalty.

summary: Cost per hour of drive time; effective only when options.objective.travel_cost = duration.
range: Integer. Default 3600. Mutually exclusive with per_km.

validationRules.text: per_hour and per_km both set -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: per_hour cost 2000 with travel_cost = duration -> route cost based on hours driven.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_hour effective when travel_cost is duration

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: per_hour 2000 + per_km 10 both set -> HTTP 400.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_hour and per_km mutually exclusive

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: default per_hour 3600 (cost per 3600 seconds = 1 hour's worth).
Interaction: with travel_cost = distance, per_hour is ineffective; solver ignores it.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_hour effective only with travel_cost = duration

summary: Cost per km of distance; effective only when options.objective.travel_cost = distance.
range: Integer. Mutually exclusive with per_hour.

validationRules.text: per_km and per_hour both set -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: per_km cost 50 with travel_cost = distance -> route cost based on km traveled.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_km effective when travel_cost is distance

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: per_km 50 + per_hour 2000 both set -> HTTP 400.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_hour and per_km mutually exclusive

testingGuidance.text: Positive: per_km 30 makes a shorter route preferred over a longer one.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_km cost incentivizes shorter routes

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: with travel_cost = duration, per_km is ineffective; solver ignores it.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_km effective only with travel_cost = distance

summary: Cost per fulfilled order (job or shipment); always added to route cost.
range: Integer.

testingGuidance.text: Behavioral: per_order cost 50 applies 50 units per fulfilled job/shipment.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_order cost per fulfilled task

testingGuidance.text: Positive: per_order cost 30 with 10 jobs on a vehicle = 300 added to route cost.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: cost scales with number of orders

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: per_order cost interacts with other cost components (fixed, per_km, per_hour) to form total route cost.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: per_order always added to total

summary: DEPRECATED — use start_depot_ids / end_depot_ids instead. Legacy single depot reference.
range: Integer. Deprecated legacy depot reference.

businessRules.text: Deprecated: prefer start_depot_ids/end_depot_ids. Retained for backward compatibility.

testingGuidance.text: Regression: confirm a legacy request using depot still behaves as expected; plan migration to start/end_depot_ids.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: deprecated but supported for backward compatibility

testingGuidance.text: Positive: depot 1 (legacy) works the same as start_depot_ids [1] + end_depot_ids [1].
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: legacy single depot maps to both start and end

summary: Depots where the vehicle may end its trip (alternative to end_index). In multi-depot scenarios, solver picks the geographically closest.
range: Array of depot id strings; each must match a defined depot.

businessRules.text: Delivery-type jobs with depots configured cannot be served by a vehicle that has only end depots.

validationRules.text: A depot id not present in depots[] -> validation error.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: end_depot_ids ["depot_A", "depot_B"] allows vehicle to return to either depot.
testingGuidance.rationale: multi-depot-reachability: vehicle can end at any listed depot

testingGuidance.text: Positive: relocation shift starting at depot A, ending at depot B via end_depot_ids ["depot_B"].
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: end depot provides return anchor

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: a job with delivery requiring end_depot_ids containing that depot must be served by vehicle with matching end depot.
testingGuidance.rationale: multi-depot-reachability: delivery-type jobs need vehicle end depots

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: when multiple end_depot_ids provided, solver picks the geographically nearest for load unloading.
testingGuidance.rationale: multi-depot-reachability: solver chooses nearest depot per cluster

summary: Index into locations.location where the vehicle must end its route. If neither end_index nor end_depot_ids is given, the route is open (ends at last task).
range: Integer in [0, len(location)). If neither end_index nor end_depot_ids is given, the vehicle ends the trip at the location of the last task on its route.

validationRules.text: end_index >= len(location) -> HTTP 400 (out of range).
end_index < 0 -> HTTP 400 (below range).
Non-integer end_index (e.g., "0" string) -> HTTP 400 type error.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: end_index == start_index (closed route, return to origin).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: closed route returns to start

testingGuidance.text: Positive: end_index 0, start_index 5 (distinct end depot).
Boundary: end_index len(locations)-1 (last valid index).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: max valid index is array length - 1

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: end_index == len(location) -> HTTP 400 (out of range).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: index must be < array length

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: end_index -1 -> HTTP 400 (below range).
Negative-validation: non-integer end_index (e.g., "0" string) -> HTTP 400 type error.
Interaction: omit end_index and end_depot_ids -> open route ends at the last served task (no return leg).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: open-end route defaults to last task

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: if end_index also references a location with high demand/penalty, the solver avoids routing there unless necessary.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: end anchor affects routing decisions

summary: Continuous-driving limit plus a mandatory rest; alternative to breaks. Only one of breaks / layover_config allowed per vehicle.
range: Object: { max_continuous_time (req), layover_duration (req), include_service_time? }. Only ONE of breaks / layover_config.

validationRules.text: Both layover_config and breaks set on the same vehicle -> HTTP 400.
Missing max_continuous_time or layover_duration -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: rest after each max_continuous_time of driving.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: mandatory rest after continuous driving

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: layover_config together with breaks -> HTTP 400.
Positive: max_continuous_time 14400, layover_duration 1800 -> 4-hour drives followed by 30-min rest.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: both fields required for layover

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: a long layover duration increases total working time; combined with max_working_time cap can breach limit.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: layover adds to working time

summary: Whether service time also counts toward continuous working time for layover scheduling. Default false (only driving counts).
range: Boolean. Default false.

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: default false (only driving counts toward continuous time).
Positive: include_service_time true makes service count toward the continuous-time limit.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: adds service to continuous-time calc

testingGuidance.text: Positive: include_service_time false; only driving time triggers layover, not service at stops.
Interaction: when include_service_time true, a route with 3 hours driving + 2 hours service = 5 hours toward continuous-time limit; crossing max_continuous_time triggers layover.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: service time added when flag is true

summary: Rest duration inserted after max_continuous_time. Required within layover_config. Added to total working time.
range: Required non-negative integer seconds.

businessRules.text: Adds to elapsed/working time and can push a route past the shift or max_working_time.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: layover_duration 2700 (45-min rest).
Boundary: layover_duration 0 (no rest; minimal interruption).
Interaction: rest time can breach max_working_time on long routes (C6).
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: layover counts toward max_working_time

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: with max_continuous_time 16200 and layover_duration 2700, a 5-hour drive triggers a 45-min rest; total working time jumps to 5h 45m.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: layover added after driving limit

summary: Soft cap on empty-travel distance on the first/last leg (meters). Cannot combine with max_depot_runs.
range: Integer meters. Cannot combine with max_depot_runs.

businessRules.text: Soft: overruns are penalized via costs.deadhead_distance_penalty, not hard-rejected.

validationRules.text: max_deadhead_distance together with max_depot_runs -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: modest deadhead cap (e.g., 5000m) keeps vehicles near demand.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: soft cap on empty legs

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: combined with max_depot_runs -> HTTP 400.
Positive: max_deadhead_distance 2000 on a vehicle starting 1500m from first job -> no penalty (under cap).
Interaction: when deadhead exceeds cap and deadhead_distance_penalty is set, cost increases per meter over.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty applies to distance beyond max

summary: Soft cap on empty-travel duration on the first/last leg (seconds). Cannot combine with max_depot_runs.
range: Integer seconds. Cannot combine with max_depot_runs.

businessRules.text: Soft: overruns are penalized via costs.deadhead_duration_penalty.

validationRules.text: max_deadhead_duration together with max_depot_runs -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: deadhead-duration cap (e.g., 600 seconds = 10 min).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: soft cap on empty-leg time

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: combined with max_depot_runs -> HTTP 400.
Positive: max_deadhead_duration 300 on a vehicle with first leg 250s -> no penalty (under cap).
Interaction: when deadhead duration exceeds cap and deadhead_duration_penalty is set, cost increases per second over.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: penalty applies to duration beyond max

summary: Maximum number of returns to depot to reload during a route. Allows small vehicles to reload and serve more demand. Default 1. Requires start_depot_ids.
range: Integer, default 1. Requires start_depot_ids. Conflicts with relations, layover_config, deadhead constraints.

constraints.text: Requires a start depot (start_depot_ids or start_index).
Cannot combine with max_deadhead_distance/duration, layover_config, relations.

validationRules.text: max_depot_runs > 1 without a start depot -> HTTP 400.
Combined with a conflicting field (layover_config, max_deadhead_distance, etc.) -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_depot_runs 2 lets a small vehicle reload and serve more demand.
Negative-validation: max_depot_runs 2 with layover_config also set -> HTTP 400.
Boundary: max_depot_runs 1 (default) -> vehicle does not reload.
Positive: max_depot_runs 3 with start_depot_ids ["depot_A"] allows two reloads (up to 3 total legs including start).
Interaction: with max_depot_runs > 1, vehicle can load more efficiently; solver schedules reloads when beneficial.

summary: Hard cap on cumulative route distance (meters). Applies to distance_matrix values if provided.
range: Non-negative integer meters. Route distance <= max_distance.

constraints.text: Non-negative integer meters; route distance <= max_distance.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_distance 100000 (100km) covers the plan.
Negative-infeasible: max_distance shorter than the leg to the nearest task -> vehicle serves nothing.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: vehicle cannot reach any task

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: route distance exactly max_distance accepted.
Negative-infeasible: a task that would push route distance past max_distance -> task reassigned/unassigned.
Interaction: max_distance caps the route; combined with max_travel_time, either can be the binding constraint.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: both are hard caps

summary: Hard cap on the number of stops on the vehicle's route (breaks/layovers not counted).
range: Non-negative integer. A shipment consumes TWO stops (pickup + delivery).

constraints.text: Served stops on the route must be <= max_stops.

businessRules.text: Tasks beyond the cap go to other vehicles or result.unassigned.
max_stops 0 makes the vehicle effectively unused.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_stops 8 with 8 eligible jobs — all served.
Boundary: 9th eligible job with max_stops 8 -> unassigned or reassigned.
Negative-infeasible: fleet cap below total eligible demand forces unassigned.
Boundary: max_stops 0 -> vehicle serves no tasks.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-stops-tasks-cap rule: zero cap = unused vehicle

testingGuidance.text: Positive: a shipment (pickup + delivery) consumes 2 stops; max_stops 4 allows 2 shipments.

summary: Hard cap on the number of tasks assignable to the vehicle (jobs and shipments each count as 1 task).
range: Positive integer; served tasks <= max_tasks.

businessRules.text: Excess tasks reassigned or unassigned. max_tasks 0 -> vehicle serves nothing.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_tasks 5, 5 jobs -> all served.
Boundary: 6th job with max_tasks 5 -> elsewhere/unassigned.
Negative-infeasible: two vehicles each max_tasks 5, 12 jobs -> >=2 unassigned.
Boundary: max_tasks 0 -> vehicle serves no tasks; effectively unused.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-stops-tasks-cap rule: zero cap = no tasks

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: max_tasks and max_stops both constrain vehicle utilization; the tighter one becomes binding.

summary: DEPRECATED — use max_distance / max_travel_time instead. Legacy cap on travel cost.
range: Integer. Deprecated legacy cap.

businessRules.text: Deprecated: prefer max_distance / max_travel_time.

testingGuidance.text: Regression: legacy max_travel_cost still parsed; plan migration to modern caps.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: deprecated but supported for backward compatibility

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_travel_cost 1800 interpreted as max_distance (if travel_cost=distance) or max_travel_time (if travel_cost=duration).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: legacy behavior depends on travel_cost mode

summary: Hard cap on cumulative DRIVING time (excludes wait/service/setup).
range: Non-negative integer seconds. Route driving time <= max_travel_time.

constraints.text: Non-negative integer seconds; route driving time <= max_travel_time.

businessRules.text: An insertion raising driving time past the cap is rejected (task routed elsewhere/unassigned).

testingGuidance.text: Positive: max_travel_time 14400 (4h) with a 3h route.
Negative-infeasible: nearest task's leg alone exceeds max_travel_time -> vehicle serves nothing.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: vehicle cannot reach any task

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: route driving time exactly max_travel_time accepted.
Interaction: long wait time for a late window does NOT count toward max_travel_time (only driving counts), but does count toward max_working_time.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: waiting excluded from max_travel_time

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: max_travel_time caps driving; combined with max_distance, either can be the binding constraint.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: both are hard caps

summary: Hard cap on total working duration: service + waiting + setup + driving all count. Unlike max_travel_time, this includes wait and service.
range: Non-negative integer seconds. Total working time <= max_working_time.

constraints.text: Non-negative integer seconds; total working time <= max_working_time.

businessRules.text: Unlike max_travel_time, waiting and service count — a long wait for a late window can breach this.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: generous max_working_time 36000 (10h) covers driving+service+wait.
Negative-infeasible: a late time window forces waiting that pushes working time past the cap -> unassigned.
Interaction: a 40-min wait for a late window pushes route end past the shift -> unassigned.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: wait inflates working time

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: vehicle with max_working_time 480 and two 30-min breaks + 8h driving -> working time 480 (hits cap, no room for service).
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: breaks count toward working time

testingGuidance.text: Positive: a job with service time 300s counts toward max_working_time even if driving time is under cap.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: service time included in working time

summary: Preferred minimum load per (delivery) stop; below it, penalties from costs apply. Soft — drives penalties, not infeasibility.
range: Array of integers, same dimensions as capacity. Delivery jobs only. Soft — drives penalties, not infeasibility.

businessRules.text: Soft constraint: shortfall triggers costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty / _unit_penalty, does not force unassignment.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: min_stop_load [5] with all deliveries >= 5 — no penalty.
Behavioral: a delivery below min_stop_load still assigned but incurs penalty.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: soft constraint, does not block

testingGuidance.text: Positive: min_stop_load [20, 100] with capacity [100, 500] discourages underutilized stops.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: soft constraint on load utilization

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: when min_stop_load [50] with costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty [10], a delivery [30] incurs (50-30)*10 = 200 penalty.
Positive: min_stop_load [5] with a single delivery [3] at 1 location + multiple grouped at another; effective load for min_stop_load is sum of grouped loads.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: grouped tasks sum for min_stop_load calc

summary: Routing profile the vehicle uses; must be defined in options.routing.profiles. Defaults to the default profile if omitted.
range: String profile name. Defaults to the default profile if omitted.

constraints.text: If set, must match a profile defined under options.routing.profiles.

validationRules.text: A profile name not defined in options.routing.profiles -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: profile 'truck' defined in options.routing.profiles.
Negative-validation: an undefined profile name -> HTTP 400.
Positive: profile 'car' with truck-specific constraints (truck_size) works if both exist.
Interaction: different vehicles with different profiles (car vs truck) can be routed via their respective networks.

summary: Zones the vehicle may NOT serve tasks in (it may still route through them).
range: Array of integer zone IDs.

businessRules.text: A task in a restricted zone cannot be assigned to this vehicle, though the vehicle may transit the zone.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: restricted_zones [3] — vehicle avoids serving zone-3 tasks but can drive through.
testingGuidance.rationale: zone-eligibility: vehicle can transit, not serve

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: every vehicle restricts the only zone a job is in -> unassigned.
Positive: restricted_zones [5, 6, 7] with allowed_zones omitted -> vehicle can serve anywhere except zones 5-7.
Interaction: a vehicle with restricted_zones [2] and allowed_zones [1, 2, 3]; it can serve zones 1 and 3 but not 2.

summary: Capability tags the vehicle provides; must be a superset of any task it serves. Empty vehicle skills can only serve tasks with empty skills.
range: Array of non-negative integers; may be empty (then it can only serve tasks with empty skills).

businessRules.text: A task is assignable to this vehicle iff task.skills is a subset of vehicle.skills.
A single high-skill vehicle can become a bottleneck under load.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle skills [1, 2] serves a job needing [2].
testingGuidance.rationale: skills-superset rule: job skills subset of vehicle

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: job needs skill 3, no vehicle has 3 -> unassigned (skill reason).
testingGuidance.rationale: skills-superset rule: no vehicle with required skill

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: empty vehicle skills can serve only empty-skill jobs.
testingGuidance.rationale: skills-superset rule: empty is subset of nothing

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle skills [1, 2, 3] serves jobs needing [1], [2], [1, 2], [3] — all subsets.
Negative-infeasible: job needs [1, 4] but vehicle only has [1, 2, 3] -> unassigned; skill 4 missing.
testingGuidance.rationale: skills-superset rule: job skill 4 not in vehicle

summary: Multiplier on travel speed; affects arrival times and duration-based cost. Greater than 1 means faster.
range: Number > 0 up to 5.0, two-decimal precision. Default 1. >1 = faster.

validationRules.text: speed_factor 0 or negative -> HTTP 400.
speed_factor > 5.0 -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: 0.01 (slowest) and 5.0 (fastest) accepted; 5.01 -> HTTP 400.
Behavioral: speed_factor 2 halves travel times, easing time-window/duration feasibility.
Positive: speed_factor 1.5 increases speed by 50%; 1-hour drive becomes 40 minutes.
Positive: speed_factor 0.5 halves speed; 1-hour drive becomes 2 hours.
Negative-validation: speed_factor 0 -> HTTP 400 (invalid).
Negative-validation: speed_factor 5.01 -> HTTP 400 (exceeds max).
Interaction: speed_factor 2 with per_hour cost 2000 means effective hourly cost halves (40-min drive = 20-min at 2x speed = reduced cost).

summary: Depots the vehicle may start from (alternative to start_index). In multi-depot scenarios, solver picks the geographically closest.
range: Array of depot id strings; each must match a defined depot.

businessRules.text: Pickup-type jobs with depots configured cannot be served by a vehicle that has only start depots.

validationRules.text: A depot id not present in depots[] -> validation error.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle starts from one of two depots nearest its cluster.
Negative-validation: start_depot_ids referencing an undefined depot -> HTTP 400.
Positive: start_depot_ids ["depot_A", "depot_B"] allows vehicle to start from either.
Negative-infeasible: a pickup job with depot_ids ["depot_C"] but no vehicle has start_depot_ids containing depot_C -> unassigned.
testingGuidance.rationale: multi-depot-reachability: pickup-type job needs vehicle start depot

testingGuidance.text: Interaction: when multiple start_depot_ids provided, solver picks the geographically nearest for load pickup.
testingGuidance.rationale: multi-depot-reachability: solver selects nearest depot per cluster

summary: Index into locations.location where the vehicle begins its route. If neither start_index nor start_depot_ids is given, the vehicle starts at its first task.
range: Integer in [0, len(location)). If neither start_index nor start_depot_ids is given, the vehicle starts at its first task.

validationRules.text: start_index >= len(location) -> HTTP 400 (out of range).
start_index < 0 -> HTTP 400 (below range).
Non-integer start_index (e.g., "0") -> HTTP 400 type error.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: start_index 0 (nominal anchor at first location).
Boundary: start_index len(locations)-1 (last valid index).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: max valid index is array length - 1

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: start_index == len(location) -> HTTP 400 (out of range).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: index must be < array length

testingGuidance.text: Negative-validation: start_index -1 -> HTTP 400 (below range).
Negative-validation: non-integer start_index like "0" -> HTTP 400 type error.
Interaction: omit both start_index and start_depot_ids -> vehicle starts at its first task (open start).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: open start defaults to first task

testingGuidance.text: Positive: start_index 5, end_index 5 (closed route, return to origin).
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: closed route to same location

summary: The vehicle's single shift window; the whole route (incl. service + waiting) must fit within it.
range: A single [start, end] pair of Unix seconds (singular — unlike task time_windows which is a 2-D array). start <= end.

businessRules.text: Route end (last arrival + service) must be <= time_window[1].
Waiting for a late task window counts toward elapsed shift time.

validationRules.text: start > end -> HTTP 400.
A 2-D array (task-style) here -> HTTP 400 (vehicle uses a single pair).
Negative Unix seconds -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: shift [32400, 61200] (09:00–17:00) comfortably fits the route.
Positive: feasible route inside a tight shift, e.g. [32400, 36000] with one nearby job.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: tight shift still feasible if route is short

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: route ending exactly at time_window[1] accepted.
Negative-validation: time_window start > end (e.g. [61200, 32400]) -> HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: a 2-D task-style array here -> HTTP 400.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: vehicle uses single [start, end] pair

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: a job forcing route end past time_window[1] -> unassigned (couples with max-duration-distance-cap).
Interaction: a long wait for a late task window pushes route end past the shift -> unassigned.

summary: Loading-compartment dimensions of the vehicle; required for it to carry tasks that specify volume.
range: Object: { width, depth, height } in meters.

businessRules.text: A vehicle WITHOUT volume cannot serve tasks that specify volume.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle volume covers a job's volume.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: vehicle must have volume if job specifies it

testingGuidance.text: Negative-infeasible: a job with volume but every vehicle lacks volume -> unassigned.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: volume required for volume-specified jobs

testingGuidance.text: Positive: vehicle volume {width: 2.5, depth: 3.0, height: 0.6} meters can accommodate cargo within those bounds.
Interaction: jobs without specified volume can be assigned to vehicles with or without volume.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: volume required only if job specifies it

summary: Vehicle compartment depth (meters).
range: Number, meters.

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: depth just fitting the deepest cargo.
Positive: depth 3.5 meters accommodates goods up to 3.5m long.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: depth is length in meters

testingGuidance.text: Positive: depth 0.0 is valid (empty compartment) but likely unintended.

summary: Vehicle compartment height (meters).
range: Number, meters.

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: height just fitting the tallest cargo.
Positive: height 2.1 meters accommodates goods up to 2.1m tall.
Positive: height 0.5 meters (low-profile vehicle) accommodates flat cargo.

summary: Vehicle compartment width (meters).
range: Number, meters.

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: width just fitting the widest cargo.
Positive: width 2.5 meters accommodates goods up to 2.5m wide.
Positive: width 1.8 meters (narrow aisle vehicle) for tight-access deliveries.

summary: Duration of a driver break (seconds). Default 0. Break duration adds to elapsed/working time.
range: Non-negative integer seconds. Default 0.

businessRules.text: Break duration adds to elapsed/working time and can push the route past the shift or max_working_time.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: service 1800 (30-min break).
Interaction: a long break inflates working time and can breach max_working_time (C6).
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: break counts toward working time

testingGuidance.text: Boundary: service 0 (no break, or instantaneous break).
Positive: service 900 (15-min break) contributes to working time.
Interaction: vehicle with max_working_time 480 and a 30-min break (1800s) leaves only 300s for driving and service combined.
testingGuidance.rationale: max-duration-distance-cap rule: break consumes working time capacity

summary: Allowed start slots for a driver break; must sit inside the vehicle's shift. Required on a break. Non-overlapping windows.
range: Required array of [start, end] Unix-second pairs; non-overlapping; each within the vehicle's time_window.

validationRules.text: A break window outside the shift -> unschedulable / infeasible.
Overlapping break windows -> HTTP 400.

testingGuidance.text: Positive: break window [43200, 46800] inside a 09:00–17:00 shift (12:00–13:00 within 09:00–17:00).
Negative-infeasible: break window entirely outside the shift.
testingGuidance.rationale: spec: break must fit within shift

testingGuidance.text: Positive: two breaks each with non-overlapping time_windows, both inside the shift.
Negative-validation: overlapping break windows [[43200, 46800], [45000, 48000]] -> HTTP 400.
Interaction: break window [43200, 46800] inside vehicle shift [32400, 61200] is feasible.
testingGuidance.rationale: time-window-feasibility rule: break window within shift
